Introduction
Let Π n be the set of all polynomials in a single variable x over the complex field C of degree at most n. Clearly, Π n is a (n + 1)-dimensional vector space over C. Define

From (1.3), we have f L (t)|x n = L|x n . So, the map L → f L (t) is a vector space isomorphic from Π n onto H. Henceforth, H is thought of as set of both formal power series and linear functionals. We call H the umbral algebra. The umbral calculus is the study of umbral algebra.

Let f (t) ∈ H. The smallest integer k for which the coefficient of t k does not vanish is called the order of f (t) and is denoted by O(f (t)) (see [11,12,16,17]). If O(f (t)) = 1, O(f (t)) = 0, then f (t) is called a delta, an invertable series, respectively. For given two power series f (t), g(t) ∈ H such that O(f (t)) = 1 and O(g(t)) = 0, there exists a unique sequence S n (x) of polynomials with g(t)(f (t)) k |S n (x) = n!δ n,k (this condition sometimes is called orthogonality type) for all n, k ≥ 0. The sequence S n (x) is called the Sheffer sequence for (g(t), f (t)) which is denoted by S n (x) ∼ (g(t), f (t)) (see [11,12,16,17]).

In the nest section we present our main theorem and its applications. More precisely, by using the orthogonality type, we write any polynomial in Π n as a linear combination of the Apostol-Euler polynomials. Several applications related to Bernoulli, Euler and Frobenius-Euler polynomials are derived.
